newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOKKER AVIATION IN AIRBUS DEAL.
newsitem.headline: FOKKER AVIATION IN AIRBUS DEAL.

text.p: European planemaking consortium Airbus said on Friday it signed memoranda of understanding with Belgium's Belairbus and Dutch Fokker Aviation on the study phase of the A3XX large aircraft project.
Airbus Industrie said the accords were signed with a view to Belairbus and Fokker Aviation, a part of Dutch group Stork , becoming risk sharing partners in the A3XX programme.
The memoranda were expected to lead to a business agreement which would represent about $2 billion in business volume for Belairbus and Fokker Aviation, Airbus said.
"This is a first step for closer cooperation between the aircraft industries of the two countries and Airbus Industrie," an Airbus statement said.
Airbus said engineers from Fokker Aviation and Belairbus will be integrated in the A3XX programme.
"Participation in this phase will allow Belairbus and Fokker Aviation to evaluate the extent of their involvement in future phases of the A3XX programme," Airbus said.
Airbus said it was continuing talks with other aerospace companies around the world, with the aim of placing up to 40 percent of the A3XX work content with risk sharing partners.
Both Fokker Aviation and Belairbus have been associate members of the Airbus consortium on specific aircraft programmes since the late seventies.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale [AERP.CN], British Aerospace Plc , Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.

Aircraft components and maintenance firm Fokker Aviation was taken over by enigineering group Stork last year from bankrupt planemaker Fokker NV, in which Daimler-Benz Aerospace held a 51 percent stake. -- Paris Newsroom +331 4221 5452
